findings.claim: The learning window is the observed score-node support [0.0, 0.49] with 50 recorded score times; the curve support audit matches this window, so no extrapolation beyond 0.49 is licensed.
The objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; coordinate contrasts are therefore proxies, not affinity labels.

For landmark_00_soft_mass the observed curve rises from about -0.37 z at t=0 to a mid-window plateau near +1.0 to +1.6 z around t=0.15-0.30, then declines to about -0.28 z at t=0.49; the first-node rate is positive (first_rate_z ~ +9.3) and the last-node rate is negative (last_rate_z ~ -10.0), i.e. a rise-then-fall shape with 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict.

Across the 20 soft-mass landmark trends, whole-window z magnitudes are small (|z| < ~0.64) and no polynomial is accepted (polynomial_accepted=false everywhere), with relative node RMSE ~0.29-0.70 and multiple sign changes; the strongest whole-window soft-mass trend is landmark_00 (z ~ +0.64), followed by landmark_07 (z ~ +0.48) and landmark_10 (z ~ +0.40).

Several soft-mass landmarks show large first-node rates that reverse by the last node (e.g. landmark_10 first_rate_z ~ +66.3 vs last_rate_z ~ -11.6; landmark_11 first_rate_z ~ -66.3 vs last_rate_z ~ +10.8; landmark_03 first_rate_z ~ -61.0 vs last_rate_z ~ +12.7), indicating early-window transient motion rather than a stable monotone drift.

hypotheses.direction: test earlier robust response to large residuals followed by baseline curvature (C1-style delta schedule) versus constant curvature (C2) at fixed dose and fixed teachers
hypotheses.falsifier: If C1 and C2 produce indistinguishable landmark_00_soft_mass trajectory contrasts and endpoint affinity under the same seeds and dose, the stage-dependent curvature is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass predicted-endpoint world-coordinate z-contrast over observed score nodes 0.0-0.49
hypotheses.scope: global reward geometry, all seeds, observed score nodes only
hypotheses.statement: A stage-dependent geometric response scale (curvature schedule) applied to the endpoint point-cloud reward may be justified because the landmark_00_soft_mass coordinate contrast is non-monotone over the observed window: it rises early and falls late, so a single constant curvature may not match both phases.

hypotheses.direction: retain smooth interpolation (smoothstep over observed score nodes) rather than introducing a discovered stage boundary
hypotheses.falsifier: If an independently stable profile shows a reproducible knot with consistent sign across batches, a hard stage boundary would be supported instead.
hypotheses.observable: whole-window z and sign_changes for soft-mass landmark trends
hypotheses.statement: Because whole-window soft-mass trends are weak and non-polynomial with multiple sign changes, a smooth gradual curvature change is preferable to a hard data-derived knot; no reproducible knot is supported by the observed curves.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are not available; only continuous curves and summary tables were read.
No decoded final affinity labels are present in role input; coordinate contrasts are proxies and cannot establish final affinity improvement.
Selection/survival evidence was not queried in this pass; no claim about descendant survival or measured final benefit is made.
The soft-mass coordinate is an untyped geometric proxy; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is attached.
